classification.difficultyReason: Justify equilateral geometry, obtain an exact diagonal and simplify the resulting cosine expression.

spec.description: Dark outline parallelogram ABCD: A upper left, B upper right, C lower right, D lower left. P is on DC nearer D. Internal segments AP and PB are drawn. AB has 9 cm above; AD has 3 cm outside left; DP has 3 cm below. The interior angle at D is labelled 60°, and angle APB is labelled x. Vertex labels lie outside the boundary. No visible parallel arrows, equality ticks or angle arcs.
spec.mathematics: AB=DC=9 cm; AD=BC=3 cm; DP=3 cm; angle ADP=60°; x=angle APB. AB parallel DC and AD parallel BC. All geometry and labels dark.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Explain why $\triangle ADP$ is equilateral, and hence find $AP$.

answer.short: $AD=DP$ and all three angles are $60^\circ$, so $\triangle ADP$ is equilateral. $AP=3\text{ cm}$.
answer.worked:
$AD=DP=3\text{ cm}$, so $\angle DAP=\angle DPA$ (base angles of an isosceles triangle).
$$\begin{align*}\angle DAP+\angle DPA&=180^\circ-60^\circ\\\angle DAP+\angle DPA&=120^\circ\\\angle DAP=\angle DPA&=60^\circ\end{align*}$$
All three angles are $60^\circ$, so $\triangle ADP$ is equilateral and $AP=3\text{ cm}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Use the cosine rule in $\triangle BCP$ to find $BP$ in exact form.

answer.worked:
$BC=AD=3\text{ cm}$ and $CP=DC-DP=9-3=6\text{ cm}$ (opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal). $\angle BCP=180^\circ-60^\circ=120^\circ$ (co-interior angles).
$$\begin{align*}BP^2&=BC^2+CP^2-2(BC)(CP)\cos\angle BCP\\BP^2&=3^2+6^2-2(3)(6)\cos120^\circ\\BP^2&=63\\BP&=3\sqrt7\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
